lede: AI measurement gaps, creator-driven search visibility, and a $350m media rebate scandal are reshaping how luxury brands buy, place, and prove the value of every ad dollar.

stories.headline: Ads Served to AI Agents Have a Measurement Problem Nobody Has Solved Yet
stories.summary: Digiday's Thursday Media Briefing reveals that while publishers like Time are now selling ads into the markdown layer of their pages — targeting AI crawlers rather than human readers — no reliable measurement standard exists to confirm whether an agent actually processed, surfaced, or acted on the sponsored content. A publisher can use Cloudflare to verify that an AI bot crawled a page containing an ad, but that is a fundamentally different signal from attribution. With 26% of ChatGPT responses already containing a sponsored ad, the gap between inventory and proof is the most urgent infrastructure problem in performance media right now.

stories.headline: Brands Are Hiring Creators Specifically to Get Cited by AI Chatbots
stories.summary: A new Digiday investigation confirms that 'AI visibility' is now a formal deliverable on creator briefs: brands including luxury-adjacent names are selecting influencers not for reach or engagement, but for how frequently they are cited inside LLM responses. Because AI chatbots crawl public content — blogs, social posts, editorial — to answer shopping queries, a creator's authentic product review can function as a backdoor recommendation engine inside ChatGPT or Perplexity. For luxury media teams, this represents a structural shift: earned media equity is now measured in LLM citation frequency, not impressions.

stories.headline: Remark AI Launches In-Home Luxury Shopping Advisor with Real-Time Virtual Try-On
stories.summary: Remark AI — the commerce intelligence platform acquired by MySize — is rolling out an 'AI shopping advisor' purpose-built for luxury brands that combines real-time virtual try-on with persistent, memory-enabled styling guidance across an entire session. Unlike static try-on tools, Remark's platform allows shoppers to stand, move, and see how fabric drapes and shifts on their body in motion, while the same AI agent maintains full context through post-purchase service interactions. The proposition targets the clienteling gap: replicating the intuition and memory of a high-end human advisor at digital scale.

stories.headline: Sony's Own Forensic Probe Backs WPP Whistleblower: $350M in Retained Rebates Alleged
stories.summary: An amended legal complaint filed by former GroupM executive Richard Foster — published days before a court hearing on WPP's bid to dismiss the suit — now alleges that Sony conducted an independent forensic investigation into WPP's media practices and reached conclusions aligned with Foster's original claims, finding that WPP wrongly retained $350m in China rebate funds while passing only $110m to clients. The filing introduces new class-action allegations of principal media double- and triple-dipping, and names WPP Media CEO Brian Lesser as a defendant in related proceedings. For luxury advertisers with significant GroupM exposure, this is the accountability reckoning that principal trading debates have been building toward for a decade.

stories.headline: Gen Z Luxury Shoppers Now Check Resale Value Before Buying New — And AI Can't Authenticate What They Find
stories.summary: Bloomberg's interview with RealReal CEO Rati Sahi Levesque reveals that more than 80% of the platform's fastest-growing cohort — Gen Z and millennials — now scan the secondary market before purchasing new luxury goods, using resale prices as a proxy for product investment value. Chanel's Classic Flap has doubled to $11,700 since 2019; Louis Vuitton ranks among the most-searched brands on the platform — underscoring how price escalation by maisons is inadvertently training a new generation to treat luxury as an asset class. Critically, Levesque told Bloomberg that AI still cannot fully replace human authenticators, flagging a hard ceiling on automation in luxury resale operations.
